PullRequest.Title: fix: do no configure XDG_DATA_HOME for snap
PullRequest.Body:
Variable was configured first in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/2d28c0a79c87c70be93dbe73fe0a18fa12e0e7e9 to avoid a crash from corrupted mime database, more context in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/230454#issuecomment-2418352959

However that didn't fix the file dialog crashes so we ended up disabling the mime database creation in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/4e7b53c5a07914c37ccba0d1211d43d7bc82f420 but the re-configured XDG_DATA_HOME was left as such.

This leads to issues seen in
1) Terminal history https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237608
2) Trash misconfigured https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/233649
3) Font configurations https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/232578


Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/233649
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237608

- [x] Additionally ensure it doesn't regress https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/230454 and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/232578

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal VS Code Snap launch on an already-seen revision
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shell launcher performs environment setup and filesystem existence checks, waits only for pre-existing asynchronous setup jobs, then replaces itself with the Electron process. The diff removes an environment copy/export and leaves the same local-share directory check and XDG_DATA_DIRS prepend, so it adds no work to this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check and, only when absent, create $SNAP_USER_DATA/.local/share.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory stat per launch and at most one mkdir for the lifetime of the directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The launcher exported XDG_DATA_HOME to this same path, then called ensure_dir_exists on it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous before Electron starts, but identical physical path and call count before and after the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replace the launcher with the VS Code Electron executable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one exec per application or URL-handler launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same exec occurred after the same launcher setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the existing application-start boundary; the changed environment is inherited but the boundary count and scheduling are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One launcher invocation; no collection or fan-out is introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Launcher setup is synchronous, existing revision cache jobs are skipped on a warm revision, and one Electron process is exec'd.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SNAP_DESKTOP_LAST_REVISION makes this the warm path. Existing directories avoid mkdir; the diff does not alter the revision key or cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no filesystem, process, IPC, or network boundary was added to warm startup by the changed hunks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Downstream libraries may consult the user's inherited/default XDG data home, but repository evidence does not establish extra call count, larger effective data, or a new hot-path operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes data-home semantics without adding startup work, frequency, fan-out, retention, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: First Snap launch after a VS Code revision update
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The launcher performs revision-scoped cache maintenance and waits for its existing asynchronous module/schema/cache compilation before exec. The diff removes synchronous recursive deletion of the Snap-local fonts directory and symlink creation; the MIME deletion still targets the same physical directory as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive deletion per new SNAP_VERSION, proportional to files in the revision-local MIME directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One rm -rf of $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime, where the launcher had just assigned XDG_DATA_HOME=$SNAP_USER_DATA/.local/share.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on update startup, but the path and multiplicity are unchanged because the old XDG_DATA_HOME value was the same literal directory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete the revision-local fonts path and recreate a symlink to the real-home fonts directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one recursive deletion and at most one symlink per revision update; now zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each changed SNAP_VERSION synchronously removed the fonts path and conditionally linked the user's fonts before continuing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff removes synchronous filesystem work from update startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compile existing GIO, schema, pixbuf, and input-module caches and wait for completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed small set of existing jobs once per revision update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same jobs and wait occurred after font and MIME maintenance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The launcher already waits for these jobs before Electron starts; the changed hunks do not add, move, or increase them.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Revision-local cache contents; the diff decreases operations by removing font cleanup and leaves MIME cleanup cardinality unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing cache compilation jobs run asynchronously but are all joined before exec. Removed font operations were synchronous; no new burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold per SNAP_VERSION through .last_revision; warm launches skip all revision update work. Cache key and negative behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the literal before/after paths and launcher ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The amount of removed font-tree work depends on the local path contents, but this uncertainty can only affect the size of an improvement, not create a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; update startup performs strictly less synchronous filesystem maintenance in the changed area.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the terminal Run Recent Command picker for a Fish shell in the Snap build
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker awaits getShellFileHistory before it finishes materializing shell-history quick-pick items. On a cold per-window lookup, fetchFishHistory performs one file read and parses the file; subsequent lookups use the in-memory shellFileHistory map.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the Fish history file selected from inherited XDG_DATA_HOME or HOME.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per Fish shell type per window after caching, not one read per command; parsing and item allocation scale with file bytes and unique commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same code read $SNAP_USER_DATA/.local/share/fish/fish_history because the launcher overrode XDG_DATA_HOME; integrated Fish shells inherited that same location and could populate it, so the diff does not establish a systematic increase in effective history cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The picker awaits the read on its cold invocation. The boundary and full-file parsing are pre-existing; the launcher diff changes which valid user data location is selected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fish history file size and unique command count, with one effective file per shell type per window after caching.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The cold read is a single awaited operation; the result is cached for later picker invocations, with no per-entry I/O or concurrency fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold lookup reads and parses once; successful and missing results are both cached in shellFileHistory until clearShellFileHistory or window lifetime ends.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-read cached call path, low confidence in any diff-caused cost increase because both before and after paths are real Fish history stores.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The host and Snap-local history files can differ in size, but the diff provides no evidence that the newly selected file is systematically larger; both can accumulate over time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: restoring the authoritative user data path does not itself prove greater frequency or effective cardinality, and the expensive operation remains a cached one-time read.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced warm startup, revision-update startup, Electron execution, and the downstream Fish-history workflow. The change removes update-time filesystem work and does not introduce a high-confidence performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
